title.zh: 卷80 列傳第45 列女
title.raw: 卷80 列傳第45 列女 Volume 80 Biographies 45: Exemplary Women

sentences.zh: 隋書卷八十列傳第四十五

translations.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 80, Biographies 45
translations.idiomatic: Book of Sui, Volume 80, Biographies 45

sentences.zh: ○列女

translations.literal: ○ Exemplary Women
translations.idiomatic: Exemplary Women

sentences.zh: 自昔貞專淑媛，布在方策者多矣。

translations.literal: From antiquity, chaste and devoted virtuous ladies recorded in historical annals have been many.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, countless chaste and virtuous women have been recorded in the historical annals.

sentences.zh: 婦人之德，雖在於溫柔，立節垂名，咸資於貞烈。

translations.literal: A woman's virtue, though residing in gentleness, establishing integrity and leaving a lasting name all depend on steadfast fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: A woman's virtue may lie in gentleness, but to establish her integrity and win lasting renown she must rely on steadfast fidelity.

sentences.zh: 溫柔，仁之本也；

translations.literal: Gentleness is the root of benevolence;
translations.idiomatic: Gentleness is the foundation of benevolence;

sentences.zh: 貞烈，義之資也。

translations.literal: steadfast fidelity is the resource of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: steadfast fidelity is what sustains righteousness.

sentences.zh: 非溫柔無以成其仁，非貞烈無以顯其義。

translations.literal: Without gentleness one cannot complete benevolence; without steadfast fidelity one cannot manifest righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Without gentleness there can be no true benevolence; without steadfast fidelity righteousness cannot be made manifest.

sentences.zh: 是以詩書所記，風俗所在，圖像丹青，流聲竹素，莫不守約以居正，殺身以成仁者也。

translations.literal: Therefore those recorded in the Odes and Documents, celebrated in local custom, depicted in paintings, and whose fame flows through written scrolls—all upheld their vows to live uprightly and gave their lives to fulfill humaneness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the women recorded in the Odes and Documents, honored in local custom, painted in portraits, and whose fame lives on in written scrolls—all kept their vows and lived uprightly, giving their lives to fulfill the demands of humaneness.

sentences.zh: 若文伯、王陵之母，白公、杞植之妻，魯之義姑，梁之高行，衛君靈主之妾，夏侯文寧之女，或抱信以含貞，或蹈忠而踐義，不以存亡易心，不以盛衰改節，其修名彰於既往，徽音傳於不朽，不亦休乎！

translations.literal: Such as the mothers of Wenbo and Wang Ling, the wives of Duke Bai and Qi Zhi, the righteous aunt of Lu, the woman of lofty conduct in Liang, the concubine of Duke Ling of Wei, and the daughter of Xiahou Wenning—some embraced faith and held to purity, others trod loyalty and practiced righteousness, not changing their hearts for life or death, not altering their integrity for prosperity or decline; their cultivated names shine in the past, their fine reputations transmit to immortality—is this not splendid!
translations.idiomatic: Consider the mothers of Wenbo and Wang Ling, the wives of Duke Bai and Qi Zhi, the righteous aunt of Lu, the woman of lofty conduct in Liang, the concubine of Duke Ling of Wei, and the daughter of Xiahou Wenning—some embraced faith and held fast to purity, others walked the path of loyalty and righteousness. None changed their hearts whether they lived or died, none altered their integrity in fortune or misfortune. Their cultivated names shine in ages past, their fine reputations endure forever—is this not splendid!

sentences.zh: 或有王公大人之妃偶，肆情於淫僻之俗，雖衣繡衣，食珍膳，坐金屋，乘玉輦，不入彤管之書，不沾良史之筆，將草木以俱落，與麋鹿而同死，可勝道哉！

translations.literal: Some consorts of kings and great men indulge in licentious and depraved customs; though they wear embroidered robes, eat fine delicacies, sit in golden chambers, and ride jade carriages, they enter not the records of the red brush, touch not the pens of good historians, and will wither like plants and die like deer in the wild—how can this be fully told!
translations.idiomatic: Some consorts of kings and great men give themselves over to licentious and depraved ways. Though they wear embroidered robes, eat fine delicacies, dwell in golden chambers, and ride jade carriages, they win no place in the historians' records and earn no mention from worthy chroniclers. They will wither like grass and die like deer in the wild—how can one even begin to recount such cases!

sentences.zh: 永言載思，實庶姬之恥也。

translations.literal: To speak of this forever and reflect upon it is truly the shame of common concubines.
translations.idiomatic: To dwell on this forever in one's thoughts is truly the shame of ordinary women.

sentences.zh: 觀夫今之靜女，各勵松筠之操，甘於玉折而蘭摧，足以無絕今古。

translations.literal: Observing the chaste women of today, each cultivates the integrity of pine and bamboo, content to be jade broken and orchids crushed—enough to be unmatched in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the chaste women of our own day: each cultivates the steadfast integrity of pine and bamboo, willing to be broken like jade or crushed like orchids—deeds unmatched in all history.

sentences.zh: 故述其雅志，以纂前代之列女雲。

translations.literal: Therefore I relate their lofty aspirations to compile the exemplary women of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore relate their lofty aspirations, compiling this account of exemplary women from former ages.

sentences.zh: ○蘭陵公主

translations.literal: ○ Princess Lanling
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling

sentences.zh: 蘭陵公主，字阿五，高祖第五女也。

translations.literal: Princess Lanling, courtesy name A'wu, was the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling, whose courtesy name was A'wu, was the fifth daughter of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 美姿儀，性婉順，好讀書，高祖于諸女中特所鍾愛。

translations.literal: She had beautiful bearing, a gentle and compliant nature, and loved reading; among all his daughters Emperor Wen especially cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: She was graceful in bearing, gentle and compliant in nature, and fond of reading. Among all his daughters, Emperor Wen cherished her above the rest.

sentences.zh: 初嫁儀同王奉孝，卒，適河東柳述，時年十八。

translations.literal: She was first married to Wang Fengxiao, an honorary attendant, who died; she then married Liu Shu of Hedong, at age eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: She was first married to Wang Fengxiao, an honorary attendant, who soon died. She then married Liu Shu of Hedong at the age of eighteen.

sentences.zh: 諸姊並驕貴，主獨折節遵於婦道，事舅姑甚謹，遇有疾病，必親奉湯藥。

translations.literal: Her elder sisters were all proud and honored, but the princess alone restrained herself and observed the way of a wife, serving her parents-in-law with great care; when they fell ill she always personally offered medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder sisters were all proud and privileged, but the princess alone humbled herself and observed the duties of a wife. She served her parents-in-law with scrupulous care, and whenever they fell ill she personally prepared and offered their medicine.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之大悅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen heard of this he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of this, he was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 由是述漸見寵遇。

translations.literal: From this Liu Shu gradually came to receive favor.
translations.idiomatic: From this Liu Shu gradually came into favor at court.

sentences.zh: 初，晉王廣欲以主配其妃弟蕭瑒，高祖初許之，後遂適述，晉王因不悅。

translations.literal: Initially Prince of Jin Yang Guang wished to match the princess to Xiao Chang, younger brother of his consort; Emperor Wen at first agreed, but later she married Liu Shu, and the Prince of Jin was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Yang Guang, Prince of Jin, had wished to marry the princess to Xiao Chang, younger brother of his consort. Emperor Wen at first agreed, but she ultimately married Liu Shu instead, and the Prince of Jin was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及述用事，彌惡之。

translations.literal: When Liu Shu came into power he hated her all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Shu came into power, he hated her all the more.

sentences.zh: 高祖既崩，述徙嶺表。

translations.literal: After Emperor Wen died, Liu Shu was exiled to the Ling region.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wen died, Liu Shu was exiled to the Ling region in the far south.

sentences.zh: 煬帝令主與述離絕，將改嫁之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang ordered the princess to sever ties with Liu Shu and intended to remarry her.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang ordered the princess to sever ties with Liu Shu and intended to marry her to someone else.

sentences.zh: 公主以死自誓，不復朝謁，上表請免主號，與述同徙。

translations.literal: The princess vowed upon her life, ceased attending court audiences, and submitted a memorial asking to be stripped of her title and exiled with Liu Shu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess swore she would rather die, ceased attending court audiences, and submitted a memorial asking to be stripped of her title and exiled together with Liu Shu.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒曰：「天下豈無男子，欲與述同徙耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and said: "Are there no men under Heaven that you wish to be exiled with Liu Shu?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and said, "Are there no men under Heaven? Do you truly wish to be exiled together with Liu Shu?

sentences.zh: 主曰：「先帝以妾適於柳家，今其有罪，妾當從坐，不願陛下屈法申恩。」

translations.literal: The princess said: "The late emperor gave me in marriage to the Liu family; now that they have committed a crime, I should share the punishment. I do not wish Your Majesty to bend the law to show me favor."
translations.idiomatic: The princess replied, "The late emperor gave me in marriage to the Liu family. Now that they have committed a crime, I ought to share their punishment. I do not wish Your Majesty to bend the law on my account.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，主憂憤而卒，時年三十二。

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent; the princess died of grief and indignation, at age thirty-two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree. The princess died of grief and indignation at the age of thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 臨終上表曰：「昔共薑自誓，著美前詩，鄎媯不言，傳芳往誥。

translations.literal: On her deathbed she submitted a memorial saying: "In former times Jiang of Gong swore her vow, winning praise in the ancient Odes; Gui of Xi remained silent, leaving fragrance in past edicts.
translations.idiomatic: On her deathbed she submitted a memorial saying, "In former times Jiang of Gong swore her vow and won praise in the ancient Odes; Gui of Xi held her silence and left her fragrance in edicts of old.

sentences.zh: 妾雖負罪，竊慕古人。

translations.literal: Though I bear guilt, I privately admire the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Though I bear guilt, I have privately admired the ancients.

sentences.zh: 生既不得從夫，死乞葬于柳氏。」

translations.literal: In life I could not follow my husband; in death I beg to be buried in the Liu clan."
translations.idiomatic: In life I could not follow my husband; in death I beg to be buried among the Liu clan.

sentences.zh: 帝覽之愈怒，竟不哭，乃葬主于洪瀆川，資送甚薄。

translations.literal: When the emperor read it he grew even angrier, and did not weep at all; he buried the princess at Hongdu Stream with very meager funeral provisions.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read this he grew even angrier. He did not weep at all, but buried the princess at Hongdu Stream with very meager funeral provisions.

sentences.zh: 朝野傷之。

translations.literal: Court and commoners alike grieved for her.
translations.idiomatic: Court and commoners alike grieved for her.

sentences.zh: 南陽公主者，煬帝之長女也。

translations.literal: Princess Nanyang was the eldest daughter of Emperor Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Nanyang was the eldest daughter of Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，有志節，造次必以禮。

translations.literal: She had fine bearing, possessed resolve and integrity, and in every circumstance observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: She had fine bearing, possessed resolve and integrity, and observed ritual propriety in every circumstance.

sentences.zh: 年十四，嫁于許國公宇文述子士及，以謹肅聞。

translations.literal: At fourteen she married Yu Shiji, son of Duke of Xu Yu Wen Shu, and was known for her careful solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen she married Yu Shiji, son of Yuwen Shu, Duke of Xu, and was known for her careful and solemn conduct.

sentences.zh: 及述病且卒，主視調飲食，手自奉上，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: When Yu Wen Shu fell ill and was near death, the princess supervised his diet and personally offered food; the world praised her for this.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Shu fell gravely ill and was near death, the princess supervised his diet and personally offered his food. The world praised her for this.

sentences.zh: 及宇文化及殺逆，主隨至聊城，而化及為竇建德所敗，士及自濟北西歸大唐。

translations.literal: When Yu Wen Huaji committed regicide, the princess followed him to Liaocheng; Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, and Shiji returned west from Jibei to the Great Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, the princess followed him to Liaocheng. Huaji was defeated by Dou Jiande, while Shiji fled west from Jibei to submit to the Great Tang.

sentences.zh: 時隋代衣冠並在其所，建德引見之，莫不惶懼失常，唯主神色自若。

translations.literal: At that time the gentry of the Sui were all in his camp; when Dou Jiande summoned them for audience, none failed to show fear and lose composure—only the princess remained calm in countenance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the gentry of the Sui were all in his camp. When Dou Jiande summoned them for an audience, everyone showed fear and lost composure—only the princess remained calm.

sentences.zh: 建德與語，主自陳國破家亡，不能報怨雪恥，淚下盈襟，聲辭不輟，情理切至。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande spoke with her; the princess declared that her state was destroyed and her house ruined, that she could not avenge wrongs and wipe away shame; tears filled her robe, her words did not cease, and her reasoning was deeply moving.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande spoke with her. The princess declared that her state was destroyed and her house ruined, that she could not avenge her wrongs and wipe away her shame. Tears filled her robe, her words did not cease, and her reasoning was deeply moving.

sentences.zh: 建德及觀聽者莫不為之動容隕涕，鹹肅然敬異焉。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande and all who watched were moved to tears; all regarded her with solemn respect and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande and all who watched were moved to tears. Everyone regarded her with solemn respect and wonder.

sentences.zh: 及建德誅化及，時主有一子，名禪師，年且十歲。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande executed Huaji, the princess had a son named Chanshi, nearly ten years old.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande executed Huaji, the princess had a son named Chanshi, nearly ten years old.

sentences.zh: 建德遣武賁郎將於士澄謂主曰：「宇文化及躬行殺逆，人神所不容。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande sent Martial Guard Commandant Yu Shicheng to tell the princess: "Yu Wen Huaji personally committed regicide, intolerable to men and spirits alike.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande sent Martial Guard Commandant Yu Shicheng to tell the princess, "Yuwen Huaji personally committed regicide—intolerable to both men and spirits.

sentences.zh: 今將族滅其家，公主之子，法當從坐，若不能割愛，亦聽留之。」

translations.literal: Now his entire clan will be exterminated; the princess's son, by law, should share the punishment. If you cannot sever affection, you may also keep him."
translations.idiomatic: Now his entire clan will be exterminated. Your son, by law, should share the punishment. If you cannot bring yourself to part with him, you may keep him.

sentences.zh: 主泣曰：「武賁既是隋室貴臣，此事何須見問！」

translations.literal: The princess wept and said: "Since the Martial Guard is a noble minister of the Sui house, why need you ask about this matter!"
translations.idiomatic: The princess wept and said, "Since you, Martial Guard, are a noble minister of the Sui house, why need you ask about this at all!

sentences.zh: 建德竟殺之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande ultimately killed the boy.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande ultimately killed the boy.

sentences.zh: 主尋請建德削髮為尼。

translations.literal: The princess soon asked Dou Jiande to let her shave her head and become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: The princess soon asked Dou Jiande to let her shave her head and become a nun.

sentences.zh: 及建德敗，將歸西京，複與士及遇於東都之下，主不與相見。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated and she was about to return to the Western Capital, she again encountered Shiji below the Eastern Capital; the princess would not meet with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande was defeated and she was about to return to the Western Capital, she again encountered Shiji below the Eastern Capital. The princess refused to meet with him.

sentences.zh: 士及就之，立於戶外，請複為夫妻。

translations.literal: Shiji went to her and stood outside the door, asking to resume their marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji went to her and stood outside the door, asking to resume their marriage.

sentences.zh: 主拒之曰：「我與君仇家。

translations.literal: The princess refused him, saying: "You and I are enemies' kin.
translations.idiomatic: The princess refused him, saying, "You and I are enemies' kin.

sentences.zh: 今恨不能手刃君者，但謀逆之日，察君不預知耳。」

translations.literal: Now the only reason I regret I cannot kill you with my own hand is that on the day of the plot I saw you had no foreknowledge of it."
translations.idiomatic: The only reason I regret I cannot kill you with my own hand is that on the day of the plot I saw you had no foreknowledge of it.

sentences.zh: 因與告絕，訶令速去。

translations.literal: She then declared an end to their relationship and rebuked him to leave quickly.
translations.idiomatic: She then declared an end to their relationship and rebuked him to leave at once.

sentences.zh: 士及固請之，主怒曰：「必欲就死，可相見也。」

translations.literal: Shiji pressed his request; the princess angrily said: "If you must seek death, then you may see me."
translations.idiomatic: Shiji pressed his request. The princess angrily said, "If you must seek death, then you may see me.

sentences.zh: 士及見其言切，知不可屈，乃拜辭而去。

translations.literal: Seeing her words were stern, Shiji knew she could not be bent, and bowed in farewell and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how stern her words were, Shiji knew she could not be moved. He bowed in farewell and departed.

sentences.zh: ○襄城王恪妃

translations.literal: ○ Consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke
translations.idiomatic: Consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke

sentences.zh: 襄城王恪妃者，河東柳氏女也。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke was a daughter of the Liu clan of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Prince Xiangcheng Yang Ke was a daughter of the Liu clan of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 父旦，循州刺史。

translations.literal: Her father Dan was governor of Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Dan was governor of Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 妃姿儀端麗，年十余，以良家子合法相，娉以為妃。

translations.literal: The consort had elegant and beautiful bearing; in her early teens, as a girl of good family with proper physiognomy, she was betrothed and made consort.
translations.idiomatic: The consort had elegant and beautiful bearing. In her early teens, as a girl of good family with proper physiognomy, she was betrothed and made consort.

sentences.zh: 未幾而恪被廢，妃修婦道，事之愈敬。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Ke was deposed; the consort observed the way of a wife and served him with even greater respect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Ke was deposed. The consort observed the duties of a wife and served him with even greater respect.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，恪複徙邊，帝令使者殺之于道。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Yang Ke was again exiled to the frontier; the emperor ordered envoys to kill him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Yang Ke was again exiled to the frontier. The emperor ordered envoys to kill him on the road.

sentences.zh: 恪與辭訣，妃曰：「若王死，妾誓不獨生。」

translations.literal: As Yang Ke took leave in farewell, the consort said: "If the prince dies, I swear I will not live alone."
translations.idiomatic: As Yang Ke took his leave in farewell, the consort said, "If the prince dies, I swear I will not live alone.

sentences.zh: 於是相對慟哭。

translations.literal: They then wept bitterly facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: They then wept bitterly facing each other.

sentences.zh: 恪既死，棺斂訖，妃謂使者曰：「妾誓與楊氏同穴。

translations.literal: After Yang Ke died and the coffin was prepared, the consort told the envoys: "I swear to share a grave with the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Ke died and the coffin was prepared, the consort told the envoys, "I swear to share a grave with the Yang clan.

sentences.zh: 若身死之後得不別埋，君之惠也。」

translations.literal: If after my death I am not buried separately, that will be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: If after my death I am not buried separately, that will be your kindness.

sentences.zh: 遂撫棺號慟，自經而卒。

translations.literal: She then beat upon the coffin and wailed, and hanged herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: She then beat upon the coffin and wailed, and hanged herself to death.

sentences.zh: 見者莫不為之涕流。

translations.literal: All who saw it wept for her.
translations.idiomatic: All who witnessed it wept for her.

sentences.zh: ○華陽王楷妃

translations.literal: ○ Consort of Prince Huayang Yang Kai
translations.idiomatic: Consort of Prince Huayang Yang Kai

sentences.zh: 華陽王楷妃者，河南元氏之女也。

translations.literal: The consort of Prince Huayang Yang Kai was a daughter of the Yuan clan of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The consort of Prince Huayang Yang Kai was a daughter of the Yuan clan of Henan.

sentences.zh: 父岩，性明敏，有氣幹。

translations.literal: Her father Yan was by nature intelligent and quick, with force of character.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Yan was by nature intelligent and quick, with force of character.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，為黃門侍郎，封龍涸縣公。

translations.literal: During the Renshou era he served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was enfeoffed as Duke of Longge County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he served as Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and was enfeoffed as Duke of Longge County.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，坐與柳述連事，除名為民，徙南海。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was implicated in Liu Shu's affair, stripped of rank and made a commoner, and exiled to Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, he was implicated in Liu Shu's affair, stripped of rank and made a commoner, and exiled to Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 後會赦，還長安。

translations.literal: Later he benefited from an amnesty and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Later he benefited from an amnesty and returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 有人譖岩逃歸，收而殺之。

translations.literal: Someone slandered Yan as having fled back; he was arrested and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered Yan as having fled back without permission. He was arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 妃有姿色，性婉順，初以選為妃。

translations.literal: The consort had beauty and grace, a gentle and compliant nature, and was initially selected as consort.
translations.idiomatic: The consort was beautiful and graceful, gentle and compliant in nature, and was initially selected as consort.

sentences.zh: 未幾而楷被幽廢，妃事楷逾謹，每見楷有憂懼之色，輒陳義理以慰諭之，楷甚敬焉。

translations.literal: Before long Yang Kai was confined and deposed; the consort served him with even greater care. Whenever she saw worry and fear on his face she would expound principles to comfort and instruct him; Yang Kai greatly respected her.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yang Kai was confined and deposed. The consort served him with even greater care. Whenever she saw worry and fear on his face she would expound moral principles to comfort and instruct him. Yang Kai greatly respected her.

sentences.zh: 及江都之亂，楷遇宇文化及之逆，以妃賜其党元武達。

translations.literal: At the turmoil of Jiangdu, Yang Kai encountered Yu Wen Huaji's rebellion; the consort was given to his follower Yuan Wuda.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil at Jiangdu, Yang Kai encountered Yuwen Huaji's rebellion. The consort was given to his follower Yuan Wuda.

sentences.zh: 武達初以宗族之禮，置之別舍，後因醉而逼之。

translations.literal: At first Yuan Wuda treated her with the rites due a clansman's wife and housed her in a separate residence; later, while drunk, he forced himself upon her.
translations.idiomatic: At first Yuan Wuda treated her with the rites due a clansman's wife and housed her in a separate residence. Later, while drunk, he tried to force himself upon her.

sentences.zh: 妃自誓不屈，武達怒，撻之百餘，辭色彌厲。

translations.literal: The consort vowed she would not yield; Yuan Wuda was enraged and flogged her more than a hundred times, yet her words and expression grew all the sterner.
translations.idiomatic: The consort vowed she would not yield. Yuan Wuda was enraged and flogged her more than a hundred times, yet her words and expression grew all the sterner.

sentences.zh: 因取甓自毀其面，血淚交下，武達釋之。

translations.literal: She then took a brick and destroyed her own face; blood and tears flowed together, and Yuan Wuda released her.
translations.idiomatic: She then took a brick and destroyed her own face. Blood and tears flowed together, and Yuan Wuda released her.

sentences.zh: 妃謂其徒曰：「我不能早死，致令將見侵辱，我之罪也。」

translations.literal: The consort said to her attendants: "I could not die early, and so was about to suffer violation—this is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: The consort said to her attendants, "I did not die sooner, and so was about to suffer violation—this is my fault.

sentences.zh: 因不食而卒。

translations.literal: She then ceased eating and died.
translations.idiomatic: She then ceased eating and died.

sentences.zh: ○譙國夫人

translations.literal: ○ Lady of Qiao
translations.idiomatic: Lady of Qiao

sentences.zh: 譙國夫人者，高涼洗氏之女也。

translations.literal: The Lady of Qiao was a daughter of the Xi clan of Gaoliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady of Qiao was a daughter of the Xi clan of Gaoliang.

sentences.zh: 世為南越首領，跨據山洞，部落十余萬家。

translations.literal: For generations her family were chieftains of the Southern Yue, holding mountain caves and commanding more than a hundred thousand households in their tribes.
translations.idiomatic: For generations her family were chieftains of the Southern Yue, holding mountain strongholds and commanding more than a hundred thousand tribal households.

sentences.zh: 夫人幼賢明，多籌略，在父母家，撫循部眾，能行軍用師，壓服諸越。

translations.literal: From youth the lady was wise and intelligent, with many stratagems; while still in her parents' home she governed and comforted her followers, could deploy troops and command armies, and subdued the various Yue peoples.
translations.idiomatic: From youth the lady was wise and intelligent, with many stratagems. While still in her parents' home she governed and comforted her followers, could deploy troops and command armies, and subdued the various Yue peoples.

sentences.zh: 每勸親族為善，由是信義結於本鄉。

translations.literal: She always urged her kin to do good, and thus faith and righteousness bound her native region.
translations.idiomatic: She always urged her kin to do good, and thus faith and righteousness bound her native region.

sentences.zh: 越人之俗，好相攻擊，夫人兄南梁州刺史挺，恃其富強，侵掠傍郡，嶺表苦之。

translations.literal: The custom of the Yue people was to attack one another; the lady's elder brother Ting, governor of Nanliangzhou, relied on his wealth and strength to raid neighboring commanderies, and the Ling region suffered from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue people were accustomed to attacking one another. The lady's elder brother Ting, governor of Nanliangzhou, relied on his wealth and strength to raid neighboring commanderies, and the Ling region suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 夫人多所規諫，由是怨隙止息，海南、儋耳歸附者千餘洞。

translations.literal: The lady often admonished him, and thus enmity ceased; more than a thousand cave-settlements of Hainan and Dan'er submitted to her.
translations.idiomatic: The lady often admonished him, and thus enmity ceased. More than a thousand cave-settlements of Hainan and Dan'er submitted to her.

sentences.zh: 梁大同初，羅州刺史馮融聞夫人有志行，為其子高涼太守寶娉以為妻。

translations.literal: In the early Datong era of Liang, Governor of Luozhou Feng Rong, hearing of the lady's resolve and conduct, betrothed her to his son Bao, governor of Gaoliang, as wife.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Datong era of Liang, Feng Rong, governor of Luozhou, hearing of the lady's resolve and conduct, betrothed her to his son Bao, governor of Gaoliang, as his wife.

sentences.zh: 融本北燕苗裔，初，馮弘之投高麗也，遣融大父業以三百人浮海歸宋，因留於新會。

translations.literal: Feng Rong was descended from Northern Yan; initially, when Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, he sent Rong's great-grandfather Ye with three hundred men to cross the sea and return to Song, and they remained at Xinhui.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Rong was descended from Northern Yan. When Feng Hong fled to Goguryeo, he sent Rong's great-grandfather Ye with three hundred men to cross the sea and submit to Song, and they settled at Xinhui.

sentences.zh: 自業及融，三世為守牧，他鄉羈旅，號令不行。

translations.literal: From Ye to Rong, for three generations they served as prefects and governors, yet as sojourners in a foreign land their orders did not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: From Ye to Rong, for three generations they served as prefects and governors, yet as sojourners in a foreign land their orders did not prevail.

sentences.zh: 至是，夫人誡約本宗，使從民禮。

translations.literal: At this point the lady admonished and restrained her own clan, making them follow the rites of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the lady admonished and restrained her own clan, making them follow the rites of the common people.

sentences.zh: 每共寶參決辭訟，首領有犯法者，雖是親族，無所舍縱。

translations.literal: She often joined Bao in deciding lawsuits; when chieftains violated the law, even if they were kin, none were spared.
translations.idiomatic: She often joined Bao in deciding lawsuits. When chieftains violated the law, even if they were kin, none were spared.

sentences.zh: 自此政令有序，人莫敢違。

translations.literal: From this government and orders were orderly, and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: From this government and orders were orderly, and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 遇侯景反，廣州都督蕭勃徵兵援台。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, Governor-General of Guangzhou Xiao Bo mobilized troops to aid the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Xiao Bo, governor-general of Guangzhou, mobilized troops to aid the capital.

sentences.zh: 高州刺史李遷仕據大皋口，遣召寶。

translations.literal: Governor of Gaozhou Li Qianshi held Dagao Pass and sent to summon Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi, governor of Gaozhou, held Dagao Pass and sent to summon Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶欲往，夫人止之曰：「刺史無故不合召太守，必欲詐君共為反耳。」

translations.literal: Bao wished to go; the lady stopped him, saying: "The governor has no reason to summon the prefect without cause—he surely intends to deceive you into joining his rebellion."
translations.idiomatic: Bao wished to go, but the lady stopped him, saying, "The governor has no reason to summon the prefect without cause—he surely intends to deceive you into joining his rebellion.

sentences.zh: 寶曰：「何以知之？」

translations.literal: Bao said: "How do you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: Bao asked, "How do you know this?

sentences.zh: 夫人曰：「刺史被召援台，乃稱有疾，鑄兵聚眾，而後喚君。

translations.literal: The lady said: "The governor was summoned to aid the capital, yet claimed illness, cast weapons and gathered troops, and only then called for you.
translations.idiomatic: The lady said, "The governor was summoned to aid the capital, yet claimed illness, cast weapons and gathered troops, and only then called for you.

sentences.zh: 今者若往，必留質，追君兵眾。

translations.literal: If you go now, he will surely hold you as hostage and press your troops into service.
translations.idiomatic: If you go now, he will surely hold you as hostage and press your troops into service.

sentences.zh: 此意可見，願且無行，以觀其勢。」

translations.literal: This intention is clear; I wish you not to go for now, to observe how matters develop."
translations.idiomatic: His intention is clear. I urge you not to go for now, but to watch how matters develop.

sentences.zh: 數日，遷仕果反，遣主帥杜平虜率兵入灨石。

translations.literal: Within days Li Qianshi did rebel, sending his chief commander Du Pinglu to lead troops into Gaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Li Qianshi did rebel, sending his chief commander Du Pinglu to lead troops into Gaoshi.

sentences.zh: 寶知之，遽告，夫人曰：「平虜，驍將也，領兵入灨石，即與官兵相拒，未得還。

translations.literal: Bao learned of it and hurried to report; the lady said: "Pinglu is a fierce general; leading troops into Gaoshi, he will immediately engage government forces and be unable to return.
translations.idiomatic: Bao learned of it and hurried to report. The lady said, "Pinglu is a fierce general. Leading troops into Gaoshi, he will immediately engage government forces and be unable to return.

sentences.zh: 遷仕在州，無能為也。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi remains in the prefecture and can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi remains in the prefecture and can do nothing.

sentences.zh: 若君自往，必有戰鬥。

translations.literal: If you go yourself, there will surely be fighting.
translations.idiomatic: If you go yourself, there will surely be fighting.

sentences.zh: 宜遣使詐之，卑辭厚禮，雲身未敢出，欲遣婦往參。

translations.literal: You should send an envoy to deceive him with humble words and rich gifts, saying you dare not go yourself and wish to send your wife to attend him.
translations.idiomatic: You should send an envoy to deceive him with humble words and rich gifts, saying you dare not go yourself and wish to send your wife to attend him.

sentences.zh: 彼聞之喜，必無防慮。

translations.literal: When he hears this he will rejoice and surely be without guard.
translations.idiomatic: When he hears this he will rejoice and surely let down his guard.

sentences.zh: 於是我將千余人，步擔雜物，唱言輸賧，得至柵下，賊必可圖。」

translations.literal: Then I shall take more than a thousand men, carrying goods on foot, proclaiming we come to pay tribute; reaching the stockade, the rebels can surely be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Then I shall take more than a thousand men, carrying goods on foot and proclaiming we come to pay tribute. Once we reach the stockade, the rebels can surely be taken.

sentences.zh: 寶從之，遷仕果大喜，覘夫人眾皆擔物，不設備。

translations.literal: Bao followed her advice; Li Qianshi was greatly pleased, and seeing the lady's followers all carrying goods, made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Bao followed her advice. Li Qianshi was greatly pleased, and seeing the lady's followers all carrying goods, made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 夫人擊之，大捷。

translations.literal: The lady attacked and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: The lady attacked and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 遷仕遂走，保于寧都。

translations.literal: Li Qianshi fled and took refuge at Ningdu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qianshi fled and took refuge at Ningdu.

sentences.zh: 夫人總兵與長城侯陳霸先會于灨石。

translations.literal: The lady commanded troops and met Marquis of Changcheng Chen Baxian at Gaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: The lady commanded troops and met Chen Baxian, Marquis of Changcheng, at Gaoshi.

sentences.zh: 還謂寶曰：「陳都督大可畏，極得眾心。

translations.literal: Returning, she told Bao: "Governor Chen is greatly to be feared; he wins the hearts of the people to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: On returning she told Bao, "Governor Chen is greatly to be feared. He wins the hearts of the people to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 我觀此人必能平賊，君宜厚資之。」

translations.literal: I observe that this man will surely be able to pacify the rebels; you should support him generously."
translations.idiomatic: I observe that this man will surely be able to pacify the rebels. You should support him generously."

sentences.zh: 及寶卒，嶺表大亂，夫人懷集百越，數州晏然。

translations.literal: When Bao died, the Ling region fell into great turmoil; the lady gathered the hundred Yue peoples, and several prefectures remained at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao died, the Ling region fell into great turmoil. The lady gathered the hundred Yue peoples, and several prefectures remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 至陳永定二年，其子僕年九歲，遺帥諸首領朝于丹陽，起家拜陽春郡守。

translations.literal: By the second year of Yongding of Chen, her son Pu was nine years old; he led the chieftains to court at Danyang and was appointed from common life as governor of Yangchun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the second year of Yongding of Chen, her son Pu was nine years old. He led the chieftains to court at Danyang and was appointed from common life as governor of Yangchun commandery.

sentences.zh: 後廣州刺史歐陽紇謀反，召僕至高安，誘與為亂。

translations.literal: Later Governor of Guangzhou Ouyang He plotted rebellion, summoning Pu to Gao'an and tempting him to join the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Later Ouyang He, governor of Guangzhou, plotted rebellion. He summoned Pu to Gao'an and tempted him to join the revolt.

sentences.zh: 僕遣使歸告夫人，夫人曰：「我為忠貞，經今兩代，不能惜汝，輒負國家。」

translations.literal: Pu sent a messenger home to tell the lady; she said: "I have served in loyalty through two dynasties now; I cannot spare you and betray the state."
translations.idiomatic: Pu sent a messenger home to tell the lady. She said, "I have served in loyalty through two dynasties now. I cannot spare you and betray the state.

sentences.zh: 遂發兵拒境，帥百越酋長迎章昭達。

translations.literal: She then mobilized troops to guard the border, leading the chieftains of the hundred Yue to welcome Zhang Zhaoda.
translations.idiomatic: She then mobilized troops to guard the border, leading the chieftains of the hundred Yue to welcome Zhang Zhaoda.

sentences.zh: 內外逼之，紇徒潰散。

translations.literal: Pressed from within and without, He's followers scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed from within and without, He's followers scattered in defeat.

sentences.zh: 僕以夫人之功，封信都侯，加平越中郎將，轉石龍太守。

translations.literal: For the lady's merit, Pu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu, promoted to General of the Center for Pacifying Yue, and transferred to governor of Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: For the lady's merit, Pu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xindu, promoted to General of the Center for Pacifying Yue, and transferred to governor of Shilong.

sentences.zh: 詔使持節冊夫人為中郎將、石龍太夫人，賚繡「Ｗ油絡駟馬安車一乘，給鼓吹一部，並麾幢旌節，其鹵簿一如刺史之儀。

translations.literal: An edict with staff of authority enfeoffed the lady as General of the Center and Grand Lady of Shilong, bestowing an embroidered-canopy carriage with four-horse team and lacquered net, one set of drums and pipes, along with banners, flags, and insignia of command; her guard of honor matched that of a governor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict with staff of authority enfeoffed the lady as General of the Center and Grand Lady of Shilong, bestowing an embroidered-canopy carriage with a four-horse team and lacquered net, one set of drums and pipes, along with banners, flags, and insignia of command. Her guard of honor matched that of a governor.

sentences.zh: 至德中，僕卒。

translations.literal: During the Zhide era, Pu died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhide era, Pu died.

sentences.zh: 後遇陳國亡，嶺南未有所附，數郡共奉夫人，號為聖母，保境安民。

translations.literal: Later when Chen fell, Lingnan had no lord to follow; several commanderies together upheld the lady, calling her the Holy Mother, and she guarded the territory and settled the people.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Chen fell, Lingnan had no lord to follow. Several commanderies together upheld the lady, calling her the Holy Mother, and she guarded the territory and settled the people.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣總管韋洸安撫嶺外，陳將徐璒以南康拒守。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen sent Commander Wei Guang to pacify the region beyond the Ling, while Chen general Xu Qiong held Nankang in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sent Commander Wei Guang to pacify the region beyond the Ling, while Chen general Xu Qiong held Nankang in defense.

sentences.zh: 洸至嶺下，逡巡不敢進。

translations.literal: When Guang reached the foot of the Ling range, he hesitated and dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang reached the foot of the Ling range, he hesitated and dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 初，夫人以扶南犀杖獻于陳主，至此，晉王廣遣陳主遺夫人書，諭以國亡，令其歸化，並以犀杖及兵符為信，夫人見杖，驗知陳亡，集首領數千，盡日慟哭。

translations.literal: Earlier the lady had presented a rhinoceros-horn staff from Funan to the Chen ruler; at this point Prince of Jin Yang Guang had the Chen ruler send the lady a letter explaining the state's fall and urging her to submit, along with the rhinoceros staff and military tally as proof. Seeing the staff, the lady verified Chen's fall, gathered several thousand chieftains, and wept in grief all day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the lady had presented a rhinoceros-horn staff from Funan to the Chen ruler. At this point Yang Guang, Prince of Jin, had the Chen ruler send the lady a letter explaining the state's fall and urging her to submit, along with the rhinoceros staff and military tally as proof. Seeing the staff, the lady verified Chen's fall, gathered several thousand chieftains, and wept in grief all day.

sentences.zh: 遣其孫魂帥眾迎洸，入至廣州，嶺南悉定。

translations.literal: She sent her grandson Hun to lead the people in welcoming Guang; he entered Guangzhou and all of Lingnan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: She sent her grandson Hun to lead the people in welcoming Guang. He entered Guangzhou and all of Lingnan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 表魂為儀同三司，冊夫人為宋康郡夫人。

translations.literal: Hun was memorialized as Honorary Attendant of the Third Rank, and the lady was enfeoffed as Lady of Songkang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was memorialized as Honorary Attendant of the Third Rank, and the lady was enfeoffed as Lady of Songkang commandery.

sentences.zh: 未幾，番禺人王仲宣反，首領皆應之，圍洸於州城，進兵屯衡嶺。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Zhongxuan of Panyu rebelled; chieftains all responded, besieging Guang at the prefectural city and advancing troops to encamp at Hengling.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Zhongxuan of Panyu rebelled. The chieftains all responded, besieging Guang at the prefectural city and advancing troops to encamp at Hengling.

sentences.zh: 夫人遣孫暄帥師救洸。

translations.literal: The lady sent her grandson Xuan to lead troops to rescue Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The lady sent her grandson Xuan to lead troops to rescue Guang.

sentences.zh: 暄與逆党陳佛智素相友善，故遲留不進。

translations.literal: Xuan had long been friendly with the rebel Chen Fozhi, and therefore delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had long been friendly with the rebel Chen Fozhi, and therefore delayed and did not advance.

sentences.zh: 夫人知之，大怒，遣使執暄，系於州獄。

translations.literal: When the lady learned of this she was furious, sent envoys to seize Xuan, and imprisoned him in the prefectural jail.
translations.idiomatic: When the lady learned of this she was furious. She sent envoys to seize Xuan and imprisoned him in the prefectural jail.

sentences.zh: 又遣孫盎出討佛智，戰克，斬之。

translations.literal: She then sent her grandson Ang to campaign against Fozhi, defeated him in battle, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: She then sent her grandson Ang to campaign against Fozhi, defeated him in battle, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 進兵至南海，與鹿願軍會，共敗仲宣。

translations.literal: Advancing to Nanhai, she joined forces with Lu Yuan's army and together defeated Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Nanhai, she joined forces with Lu Yuan's army and together defeated Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 夫人親被甲，乘介馬，張錦傘，領彀騎，衛詔使裴矩巡撫諸州，其蒼梧首領陳坦、岡州馮岑翁、梁化鄧馬頭、藤州李光略、羅州龐靖等皆來參謁。

translations.literal: The lady personally donned armor, rode an armored horse, spread a brocade parasol, and led armored cavalry to escort Imperial Commissioner Pei Ju on his tour of the prefectures; chieftains Chen Tan of Cangwu, Feng Cenweng of Gangzhou, Deng Matou of Lianghua, Li Guanglue of Tengzhou, Pang Jing of Luozhou, and others all came to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: The lady personally donned armor, rode an armored horse, spread a brocade parasol, and led armored cavalry to escort Imperial Commissioner Pei Ju on his tour of the prefectures. Chieftains Chen Tan of Cangwu, Feng Cenweng of Gangzhou, Deng Matou of Lianghua, Li Guanglue of Tengzhou, Pang Jing of Luozhou, and others all came to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 還令統其部落，嶺表遂定。

translations.literal: She then ordered them to govern their tribes, and the Ling region was settled.
translations.idiomatic: She then ordered them to govern their tribes, and the Ling region was settled.

sentences.zh: 高祖異之，拜盎為高州刺史，仍赦出暄，拜羅州刺史。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen marveled at this, appointing Ang governor of Gaozhou and releasing Xuan from prison to appoint him governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen marveled at this, appointing Ang governor of Gaozhou and releasing Xuan from prison to appoint him governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 追贈寶為廣州總管、譙國公，冊夫人為譙國夫人。

translations.literal: Bao was posthumously honored as Commander of Guangzhou and Duke of Qiao; the lady was enfeoffed as Lady of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was posthumously honored as Commander of Guangzhou and Duke of Qiao, and the lady was enfeoffed as Lady of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 以宋康邑回授僕妾洗氏。

translations.literal: The fief of Songkang was transferred back to Pu's concubine, Lady Xi.
translations.idiomatic: The fief of Songkang was transferred back to Pu's concubine, Lady Xi.

sentences.zh: 仍開譙國夫人幕府，置長史以下官屬，給印章，聽發部落六州兵馬，若有機急，便宜行事。

translations.literal: A staff office for the Lady of Qiao was established with officials from Chief Administrator downward, seals were granted, and she was authorized to mobilize tribal troops from six prefectures; in urgent matters she might act at her discretion.
translations.idiomatic: A staff office for the Lady of Qiao was established with officials from Chief Administrator downward. Seals were granted, and she was authorized to mobilize tribal troops from six prefectures. In urgent matters she might act at her discretion.

sentences.zh: 降敕書曰：「朕撫育蒼生，情均父母，欲使率土清淨，兆庶安樂。

translations.literal: An edict was issued saying: "We nurture the people with affection equal to that of parents, wishing to make all the realm pure and the multitude secure and content.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued saying, "We nurture the people with affection equal to that of parents, wishing to make all the realm pure and the multitude secure and content.

sentences.zh: 而王仲宣等輒相聚結，擾亂彼民，所以遣往誅翦，為百姓除害。

translations.literal: Yet Wang Zhongxuan and others rashly gathered and banded together, disturbing those people; therefore We sent forces to suppress and eliminate them, removing harm for the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wang Zhongxuan and others rashly gathered and banded together, disturbing the people. Therefore We sent forces to suppress and eliminate them, removing harm for the common people.

sentences.zh: 夫人情在奉國，深識正理，遂令孫盎斬獲佛智，竟破群賊，甚有大功。

translations.literal: The lady's heart lies in serving the state; deeply knowing what is right, she had her grandson Ang slay and capture Fozhi, ultimately breaking the rebel bands—great merit indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The lady's heart lies in serving the state. Deeply knowing what is right, she had her grandson Ang slay and capture Fozhi, ultimately breaking the rebel bands—great merit indeed.

sentences.zh: 今賜夫人物五千段。

translations.literal: Now We bestow upon the lady five thousand bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Now We bestow upon the lady five thousand bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 暄不進愆，誠合罪責，以夫人立此誠效，故特原免。

translations.literal: Xuan's failure to advance was indeed deserving of punishment, but because the lady has shown such loyal merit, he is specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's failure to advance was indeed deserving of punishment, but because the lady has shown such loyal merit, he is specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 夫人宜訓導子孫，敦崇禮教，遵奉朝化，以副朕心。」

translations.literal: The lady should instruct and guide her descendants, honor ritual teaching, and follow the court's civilizing influence, to accord with Our heart."
translations.idiomatic: The lady should instruct and guide her descendants, honor ritual teaching, and follow the court's civilizing influence, to accord with Our wishes.

sentences.zh: 皇后以首飾及宴服一襲賜之，夫人並盛于金篋，並梁、陳賜物各藏於一庫。

translations.literal: The empress bestowed upon her head ornaments and one set of banquet robes; the lady stored them all in a golden casket, and gifts from Liang and Chen were each kept in separate storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bestowed upon her head ornaments and one set of banquet robes. The lady stored them all in a golden casket, and gifts from Liang and Chen were each kept in separate storehouses.

sentences.zh: 每歲時大會，皆陳於庭，以示子孫，曰：「汝等宜盡赤心向天子。

translations.literal: At each year's great assembly she displayed them in the courtyard to show her descendants, saying: "You should devote your whole hearts to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At each year's great assembly she displayed them in the courtyard to show her descendants, saying, "You should devote your whole hearts to the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 我事三代主，唯用一好心。

translations.literal: I have served three generations of rulers with but one loyal heart.
translations.idiomatic: I have served three generations of rulers with but one loyal heart.

sentences.zh: 今賜物具存，此忠孝之報也，願汝皆思念之。」

translations.literal: Now these gifts remain intact—this is the reward of loyalty and filial piety; I wish you all to keep them in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Now these gifts remain intact—this is the reward of loyalty and filial piety. I wish you all to keep them in mind."

sentences.zh: 時番州總管趙訥貪虐，諸俚獠多有亡叛。

translations.literal: At that time Commander of Fanzhou Zhao Ne was greedy and cruel, and many of the Li and Liao peoples fled or rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhao Ne, commander of Fanzhou, was greedy and cruel, and many of the Li and Liao peoples fled or rebelled.

sentences.zh: 夫人遣長史張融上封事，論安撫之宜，並言訥罪狀，不可以招懷遠人。

translations.literal: The lady sent Chief Administrator Zhang Rong to submit a sealed memorial on the proper methods of pacification, also stating Ne's crimes and that he could not win over distant peoples.
translations.idiomatic: The lady sent Chief Administrator Zhang Rong to submit a sealed memorial on the proper methods of pacification, also stating Ne's crimes and that he could not win over distant peoples.

sentences.zh: 上遣推訥，得其贓賄，竟致於法。

translations.literal: The emperor sent to investigate Ne, found evidence of bribery, and ultimately punished him by law.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent to investigate Ne, found evidence of bribery, and ultimately punished him by law.

sentences.zh: 降敕委夫人招慰亡叛。

translations.literal: An edict was issued commissioning the lady to summon and comfort those who had fled or rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued commissioning the lady to summon and comfort those who had fled or rebelled.

sentences.zh: 夫人親載詔書，自稱使者，曆十余州，宣述上意，諭諸俚獠，所至皆降。

translations.literal: The lady personally carried the edict, calling herself an envoy; passing through more than ten prefectures she proclaimed the emperor's intent and instructed the Li and Liao peoples; wherever she went, all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The lady personally carried the edict, calling herself an envoy. Passing through more than ten prefectures she proclaimed the emperor's intent and instructed the Li and Liao peoples. Wherever she went, all submitted.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉之，賜夫人臨振縣湯沐邑，一千五百戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised her and granted the lady a bath-fief at Linzhen county of one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen praised her and granted the lady a bath-fief at Linzhen county of one thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 贈僕為岩州總管、平原郡公。

translations.literal: Pu was posthumously honored as Commander of Yanzhou and Duke of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was posthumously honored as Commander of Yanzhou and Duke of Pingyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，卒，賻物一千段，諡為誠敬夫人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou she died; funeral goods of one thousand bolts were granted, and she was given the posthumous title Lady of Sincere Reverence.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renshou she died. Funeral goods of one thousand bolts were granted, and she was given the posthumous title Lady of Sincere Reverence.

sentences.zh: ○鄭善果母

translations.literal: ○ Mother of Zheng Shanguo
translations.idiomatic: Mother of Zheng Shanguo

sentences.zh: 鄭善果母者，清河崔氏之女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Zheng Shanguo was a daughter of the Cui clan of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Zheng Shanguo was a daughter of the Cui clan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 年十三，出適鄭誠，生善果。

translations.literal: At thirteen she was given in marriage to Zheng Cheng and bore Shanguo.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen she was given in marriage to Zheng Cheng and bore Shanguo.

sentences.zh: 而誠討尉迥，力戰死於陣。

translations.literal: Cheng campaigned against Yuwen Jiong and died fighting fiercely in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng campaigned against Yuwen Jiong and died fighting fiercely in battle.

sentences.zh: 母年二十而寡，父彥穆欲奪其志，母抱善果謂彥穆曰：「婦人無再見男子之義。

translations.literal: The mother was widowed at twenty; her father Yanmu wished to change her resolve; holding Shanguo she told Yanmu: "A woman has no principle of seeing another man.
translations.idiomatic: The mother was widowed at twenty. Her father Yanmu wished to change her resolve. Holding Shanguo, she told Yanmu, "A woman has no principle of seeing another man.

sentences.zh: 且鄭君雖死，幸有此兒。

translations.literal: Moreover, though Lord Zheng is dead, fortunately there is this son.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though Lord Zheng is dead, fortunately there is this son.

sentences.zh: 棄兒為不慈，背死為無禮。

translations.literal: To abandon the child is to be unloving; to betray the dead is to be without propriety.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the child is to be unloving; to betray the dead is to be without propriety.

sentences.zh: 寧當割耳截發以明素心。

translations.literal: I would rather cut off my ears and shear my hair to declare my pure heart.
translations.idiomatic: I would rather cut off my ears and shear my hair to declare my pure heart.

sentences.zh: 違禮滅慈，非敢聞命。」

translations.literal: To violate propriety and extinguish love—I dare not accept such a command."
translations.idiomatic: To violate propriety and extinguish love—I dare not accept such a command.

sentences.zh: 善果以父死王事，年數歲，拜使持節、大將軍，襲爵開封縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: Shanguo, because his father died in the service of the state, at several years of age was appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Grand General, inheriting the title Duke of Kaifeng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo, because his father died in the service of the state, was at several years of age appointed Bearer of the Staff of Authority and Grand General, inheriting the title Duke of Kaifeng county with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，進封武德郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was advanced to Duke of Wude commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was advanced to Duke of Wude commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十四，授沂州刺史，轉景州刺史，尋為魯郡太守。

translations.literal: At fourteen he was appointed governor of Yizhou, transferred to governor of Jingzhou, and soon made governor of Lu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was appointed governor of Yizhou, transferred to governor of Jingzhou, and soon made governor of Lu commandery.

sentences.zh: 母性賢明，有節操，博涉書史，通曉治方。

translations.literal: The mother was by nature wise and intelligent, with integrity of character; she broadly studied books and histories and understood methods of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The mother was by nature wise and intelligent, with integrity of character. She broadly studied books and histories and understood methods of governance.

sentences.zh: 每善果出聽事，母恆坐胡床，於鄣後察之。

translations.literal: Whenever Shanguo went out to the audience hall, the mother always sat on a camp stool behind a screen to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Shanguo went out to the audience hall, the mother always sat on a camp stool behind a screen to observe him.

sentences.zh: 聞其剖斷合理，歸則大悅，即賜之坐，相對談笑。

translations.literal: Hearing that his judgments were reasonable, she would return greatly pleased, grant him a seat, and converse and laugh together.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that his judgments were reasonable, she would return greatly pleased, grant him a seat, and converse and laugh together.

sentences.zh: 若行事不允，或妄瞋怒，母乃還堂，蒙被而泣，終日不食。

translations.literal: If his conduct was improper or he rashly grew angry, the mother would return to her chamber, cover herself with a quilt and weep, and eat nothing all day.
translations.idiomatic: If his conduct was improper or he rashly grew angry, the mother would return to her chamber, cover herself with a quilt and weep, and eat nothing all day.

sentences.zh: 善果伏於床前，亦不敢起。

translations.literal: Shanguo would prostrate himself before her bed and dared not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo would prostrate himself before her bed and dared not rise.

sentences.zh: 母方起謂之曰：「吾非怒汝，乃愧汝家耳。

translations.literal: When the mother finally rose she told him: "I am not angry with you; I am ashamed for your family.
translations.idiomatic: When the mother finally rose she told him, "I am not angry with you; I am ashamed for your family.

sentences.zh: 吾為汝家婦，獲奉灑掃，如汝先君，忠勤之士也，在官清恪，未嘗問私，以身徇國，繼之以死，吾亦望汝副其此心。

translations.literal: I became a wife in your family and was able to serve in household duties; your late father was a man of loyalty and diligence, upright and scrupulous in office, never pursuing private interests, giving his body for the state and following with his death—I also hoped you would match this heart.
translations.idiomatic: I became a wife in your family and was able to serve in household duties. Your late father was a man of loyalty and diligence, upright and scrupulous in office, never pursuing private interests, giving his body for the state and following with his death. I also hoped you would match this heart.

sentences.zh: 汝既年小而孤，吾寡婦耳，有慈無威，使汝不知禮訓，何可負荷忠臣之業乎？

translations.literal: You were young and orphaned; I am but a widow—with love but without authority, letting you not know ritual training—how could you bear the work of a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: You were young and orphaned; I am but a widow—with love but without authority, letting you not know ritual training. How could you bear the work of a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 汝自童子承襲茅土，位至方伯，豈汝身致之邪？

translations.literal: From childhood you inherited a fief and rose to the rank of regional governor—did you achieve this by your own efforts?
translations.idiomatic: From childhood you inherited a fief and rose to the rank of regional governor—did you achieve this by your own efforts?

sentences.zh: 安可不思此事而妄加瞋怒，心緣驕樂，墮於公政！

translations.literal: How can you not reflect on this and rashly give way to anger, letting your heart be swayed by pride and pleasure, and fall short in public affairs!
translations.idiomatic: How can you not reflect on this and rashly give way to anger, letting your heart be swayed by pride and pleasure, and fall short in public affairs!

sentences.zh: 內則墜爾家風，或亡失官爵，外則虧天子之法，以取罪戾。

translations.literal: Within, you would ruin your family's reputation and perhaps lose rank and title; without, you would violate the Son of Heaven's laws and incur punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Within, you would ruin your family's reputation and perhaps lose rank and title; without, you would violate the Son of Heaven's laws and incur punishment.

sentences.zh: 吾死之日，亦何面目見汝先人於地下乎？」

translations.literal: On the day I die, with what face could I meet your ancestors in the underworld?"
translations.idiomatic: On the day I die, with what face could I meet your ancestors in the underworld?"

sentences.zh: 母恆自紡績，夜分而寐。

translations.literal: The mother always spun and wove herself, sleeping only after midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The mother always spun and wove herself, sleeping only after midnight.

sentences.zh: 善果曰：「兒封侯開國，位居三品，秩俸幸足，母何自勤如是邪？」

translations.literal: Shanguo said: "Your son is a enfeoffed marquis with a fief, holding third-rank position; salary and stipends are sufficient—why do you toil so yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo said, "Your son is an enfeoffed marquis with a fief, holding third-rank position. Salary and stipends are sufficient—why do you toil so yourself?

sentences.zh: 答曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: She replied: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: She replied, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 汝年已長，吾謂汝知天下之理，今聞此言，故猶未也。

translations.literal: You are already grown; I thought you knew the principles of the world—hearing these words now, you clearly do not yet.
translations.idiomatic: You are already grown. I thought you knew the principles of the world—hearing these words now, you clearly do not yet.

sentences.zh: 至於公事，何由濟乎？

translations.literal: As for public affairs, how could you succeed?
translations.idiomatic: As for public affairs, how could you succeed?

sentences.zh: 今此秩俸，乃是天子報爾先人之徇命也。

translations.literal: This salary and stipend now is the Son of Heaven's reward for your forebear's death in service.
translations.idiomatic: This salary and stipend now is the Son of Heaven's reward for your forebear's death in service.

sentences.zh: 當須散贍六姻，為先君之惠，妻子奈何獨擅其利，以為富貴哉！

translations.literal: You should distribute it to support the six kinds of kin, as your late father's kindness—how can wife and children alone monopolize the benefit and call themselves wealthy and honored!
translations.idiomatic: You should distribute it to support the six kinds of kin, as your late father's kindness. How can wife and children alone monopolize the benefit and call themselves wealthy and honored!

sentences.zh: 又絲枲紡織，婦人之務，上自王后，下至大夫士妻，各有所制。

translations.literal: Moreover, spinning hemp and silk is a woman's duty; from the queen above to the wives of grandees and officers below, each has her proper standards.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, spinning hemp and silk is a woman's duty. From the queen above to the wives of grandees and officers below, each has her proper standards.

sentences.zh: 若墮業者，是為驕逸。

translations.literal: To abandon this work is to be proud and indulgent.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon this work is to be proud and indulgent.

sentences.zh: 吾雖不知禮，其可自敗名乎？」

translations.literal: Though I may not know ritual, how could I ruin my own reputation?"
translations.idiomatic: Though I may not know ritual, how could I ruin my own reputation?

sentences.zh: 自初寡，便不禦脂粉，常服大練。

translations.literal: From the time she first became a widow she wore no cosmetics and always dressed in plain white silk.
translations.idiomatic: From the time she first became a widow she wore no cosmetics and always dressed in plain white silk.

sentences.zh: 性又節儉，非祭禮賓客之事，酒肉不妄陳於前。

translations.literal: Her nature was also frugal; except for sacrificial rites and entertaining guests, wine and meat were never casually set before her.
translations.idiomatic: Her nature was also frugal. Except for sacrificial rites and entertaining guests, wine and meat were never casually set before her.

sentences.zh: 靜室端居，未嘗輒出門閣。

translations.literal: She dwelt quietly in her chamber and never casually went beyond the gate.
translations.idiomatic: She dwelt quietly in her chamber and never casually went beyond the gate.

sentences.zh: 內外姻戚有吉凶事，但厚加贈遺，皆不詣其家。

translations.literal: When kin within and without had occasions of fortune or misfortune, she only sent generous gifts and never visited their homes.
translations.idiomatic: When kin within and without had occasions of fortune or misfortune, she only sent generous gifts and never visited their homes.

sentences.zh: 非自手作及莊園祿賜所得，雖親族禮遺，悉不許入門。

translations.literal: What was not earned by her own hand or from estate and salary stipends—even gifts from kin by ritual—was not permitted to enter her door.
translations.idiomatic: What was not earned by her own hand or from estate and salary stipends—even gifts from kin by ritual—was not permitted to enter her door.

sentences.zh: 善果歷任州郡，唯內自出饌，於衙中食之，公廨所供，皆不許受，悉用修治廨宇及分給僚佐。

translations.literal: Serving in successive prefectures and commanderies, Shanguo ate only food prepared within his household in the yamen; supplies from the government offices he never accepted, using them all to repair official buildings and distribute to subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Serving in successive prefectures and commanderies, Shanguo ate only food prepared within his household in the yamen. Supplies from the government offices he never accepted, using them all to repair official buildings and distribute to subordinates.

sentences.zh: 善果亦由此克己，號為清吏。

translations.literal: Shanguo also through this restrained himself and was called an upright official.
translations.idiomatic: Shanguo also through this restrained himself and was known as an upright official.

sentences.zh: 煬帝遣御史大夫張衡勞之，考為天下最。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang sent Censor-in-Chief Zhang Heng to commend him; in evaluation he was ranked foremost in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang sent Censor-in-Chief Zhang Heng to commend him, and in official evaluation he was ranked the foremost official in the realm.

sentences.zh: 征授光祿卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Director of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 其母卒後，善果為大理卿，漸驕恣，清公平允遂不如疇昔焉。

translations.literal: After his mother died, Shanguo served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and gradually grew proud and willful; his uprightness and fairness were no longer as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, Shanguo served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review and gradually grew proud and willful. His uprightness and fairness were no longer what they had once been.

sentences.zh: ○孝女王舜

translations.literal: ○ Filial Daughter Wang Shun
translations.idiomatic: Filial Daughter Wang Shun

sentences.zh: 孝女王舜者，趙郡王子春之女也。

translations.literal: The filial daughter Wang Shun was a daughter of Wang Zichun of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The filial daughter Wang Shun was a daughter of Wang Zichun of Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 子春與從兄長忻不協，屬齊滅之際，長忻與其妻同謀殺子春。

translations.literal: Zichun was at odds with his cousin Chang Xin; at the time of Northern Qi's fall, Chang Xin and his wife together plotted to kill Zichun.
translations.idiomatic: Zichun was at odds with his cousin Chang Xin. At the time of Northern Qi's fall, Chang Xin and his wife together plotted to kill Zichun.

sentences.zh: 舜時年七歲，有二妹，粲年五歲，璠年二歲，並孤苦，寄食親戚。

translations.literal: Shun was then seven years old, with two younger sisters—Can at five and Fan at two—all orphaned and dependent, living on the charity of relatives.
translations.idiomatic: Shun was then seven years old, with two younger sisters—Can at five and Fan at two—all orphaned and dependent, living on the charity of relatives.

sentences.zh: 舜撫育二妹，恩義甚篤。

translations.literal: Shun raised her two sisters with deep affection and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Shun raised her two sisters with deep affection and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 而舜陰有復仇之心，長忻殊不為備。

translations.literal: Yet Shun secretly harbored thoughts of revenge, while Chang Xin was wholly unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shun secretly harbored thoughts of revenge, while Chang Xin was wholly unprepared.

sentences.zh: 姊妹俱長，親戚欲嫁之，輒拒不從。

translations.literal: When the sisters all came of age, relatives wished to marry them off, but they always refused.
translations.idiomatic: When the sisters all came of age, relatives wished to marry them off, but they always refused.

sentences.zh: 乃密謂其二妹曰：「我無兄弟，致使父仇不復。

translations.literal: She then secretly told her two sisters: "I have no brothers, and so our father's death goes unavenged.
translations.idiomatic: She then secretly told her two sisters, "I have no brothers, and so our father's death goes unavenged.

sentences.zh: 吾輩雖是女子，何用生為？

translations.literal: Though we are women, what use is there in living?
translations.idiomatic: Though we are women, what use is there in living?

sentences.zh: 我欲共汝報復，汝意如何？」

translations.literal: I wish to take revenge together with you—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I wish to take revenge together with you—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 二妹皆垂泣曰：「唯姊所命。」

translations.literal: Both sisters wept and said: "We obey whatever our elder sister commands."
translations.idiomatic: Both sisters wept and said, "We obey whatever our elder sister commands.

sentences.zh: 是夜，姊妹各持刀逾牆而入，手殺長忻夫妻，以告父墓。

translations.literal: That night the sisters each took a knife, climbed over the wall, and personally killed Chang Xin and his wife, then reported it at their father's grave.
translations.idiomatic: That night the sisters each took a knife, climbed over the wall, and personally killed Chang Xin and his wife, then reported it at their father's grave.

sentences.zh: 因詣縣請罪，姊妹爭為謀首，州縣不能決。

translations.literal: They then went to the county to confess their crime; the sisters each claimed to be the chief plotter, and prefecture and county could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: They then went to the county to confess their crime. The sisters each claimed to be the chief plotter, and prefecture and county could not decide.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉歎，特原其罪。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and praised them with admiration, specially pardoning their crime.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of this he praised them with admiration and specially pardoned their crime.

sentences.zh: ○韓覬妻

translations.literal: ○ Wife of Han Qi
translations.idiomatic: Wife of Han Qi

sentences.zh: 韓覬妻者，洛陽於氏女也，字茂德，父實，周大左輔。

translations.literal: The wife of Han Qi was a daughter of the Yu clan of Luoyang, courtesy name Maode; her father Shi was Grand Left Assistant of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Han Qi was a daughter of the Yu clan of Luoyang, whose courtesy name was Maode. Her father Shi was Grand Left Assistant of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 於氏年十四，適於覬。

translations.literal: Lady Yu was fourteen when she married Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yu was fourteen when she married Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 雖生長膏腴，家門鼎盛，而動遵禮度，躬自儉約，宗黨敬之。

translations.literal: Though she grew up in wealth and her family gate was flourishing, in conduct she always observed ritual propriety and personally practiced frugality; her clan respected her.
translations.idiomatic: Though she grew up in wealth and her family was flourishing, in conduct she always observed ritual propriety and personally practiced frugality. Her clan respected her.

sentences.zh: 年十八，覬從軍戰沒，於氏哀毀骨立，慟感行路。

translations.literal: At eighteen Han Qi died in battle on campaign; Lady Yu's grief wasted her to skin and bone, and her mourning moved passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen Han Qi died in battle on campaign. Lady Yu's grief wasted her to skin and bone, and her mourning moved passersby on the road.

sentences.zh: 每至朝夕奠祭，皆手自捧持。

translations.literal: At each morning and evening offering she always personally held the vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At each morning and evening offering she always personally held the vessels.

sentences.zh: 及免喪，其父以其幼少無子，將嫁之。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, her father, because she was young and childless, intended to marry her off again.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, her father, because she was young and childless, intended to marry her off again.

sentences.zh: 誓無異志。

translations.literal: She swore she would not change her resolve.
translations.idiomatic: She swore she would not change her resolve.

sentences.zh: 複令家人敦喻，於氏盡夜涕泣，截發自誓。

translations.literal: Her family again earnestly urged her; Lady Yu wept all night, cut off her hair, and swore her vow.
translations.idiomatic: Her family again earnestly urged her. Lady Yu wept all night, cut off her hair, and swore her vow.

sentences.zh: 其父喟然傷感，遂不奪其志焉。

translations.literal: Her father sighed with emotion and did not force her to change her mind.
translations.idiomatic: Her father sighed with emotion and did not force her to change her mind.

sentences.zh: 因養夫之孽子世隆為嗣，身自撫育，愛同己生，訓導有方，卒能成立。

translations.literal: She then raised her husband's illegitimate son Shilong as heir, personally nurturing him with love equal to a child of her own, instructing him with proper methods until he was fully established.
translations.idiomatic: She then raised her husband's illegitimate son Shilong as heir, personally nurturing him with love equal to a child of her own and instructing him with proper methods until he was fully established.

sentences.zh: 自孀居已後，唯時或歸寧，至於親族之家，絕不來往。

translations.literal: After she became a widow she only occasionally returned to her parents' home; as for the homes of relatives, she never visited at all.
translations.idiomatic: After she became a widow she only occasionally returned to her parents' home. As for the homes of relatives, she never visited at all.

sentences.zh: 有尊卑就省謁者，送迎皆不出戶庭。

translations.literal: When seniors or juniors came to pay respects, she never went beyond the gate to see them off or welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When seniors or juniors came to pay respects, she never went beyond the gate to see them off or welcome them.

sentences.zh: 蔬食布衣，不聽聲樂，以此終身。

translations.literal: She ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, listened to no music, and lived thus to the end of her life.
translations.idiomatic: She ate plain food and wore coarse cloth, listened to no music, and lived thus to the end of her life.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞而嘉歎，下詔褒美，表其門閭，長安中號為節婦闕。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen heard and praised her with admiration, issued an edict commending her, and honored her household gate; in Chang'an she was called the Arch of the Chaste Wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen heard of this he praised her with admiration, issued an edict commending her, and honored her household gate. In Chang'an she was called the Arch of the Chaste Wife.

sentences.zh: 終於家，年七十二。

translations.literal: She died at home at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: She died at home at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: ○陸讓母

translations.literal: ○ Mother of Lu Rang
translations.idiomatic: Mother of Lu Rang

sentences.zh: 陸讓母者，上党馮氏女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Lu Rang was a daughter of the Feng clan of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Lu Rang was a daughter of the Feng clan of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 性仁愛，有母儀，讓即其孽子也。

translations.literal: She was by nature benevolent and loving, with the bearing of a mother; Rang was her stepson.
translations.idiomatic: She was by nature benevolent and loving, with the bearing of a mother. Rang was her stepson.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，為番州刺史，數有聚斂，贓貨狼籍，為司馬所奏。

translations.literal: During Renshou he served as governor of Fanzhou, repeatedly extorting wealth; booty lay scattered everywhere, and he was impeached by the Vice Governor.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he served as governor of Fanzhou, repeatedly extorting wealth until booty lay scattered everywhere. He was impeached by the Vice Governor.

sentences.zh: 上遣使按之皆驗，於是囚詣長髮，親臨問。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to investigate and all was verified; he was then imprisoned and brought to Chang'an, where the emperor personally questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to investigate and all was verified. He was then imprisoned and brought to Chang'an, where the emperor personally questioned him.

sentences.zh: 讓稱冤，上複令治書侍御史撫按之，狀不易前。

translations.literal: Rang claimed he was wronged; the emperor again ordered the Drafting Attendant Censor to reinvestigate, but the facts did not change from before.
translations.idiomatic: Rang claimed he was wronged. The emperor again ordered the Drafting Attendant Censor to reinvestigate, but the facts did not change from before.

sentences.zh: 乃命公卿百僚議之，鹹曰「讓罪當死」。

translations.literal: He then ordered the grandees and hundred officials to deliberate; all said "Rang's crime deserves death."
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the grandees and hundred officials to deliberate. All said, "Rang's crime deserves death."

sentences.zh: 詔可其奏。

translations.literal: An edict approved their memorial.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved their memorial.

sentences.zh: 讓將就刑，馮氏蓬頭垢面詣朝堂數讓曰：「無汗馬之勞，致位刺史，不能盡誠奉國，以答鴻恩，而反違犯憲章，贓貨狼籍。

translations.literal: As Rang was about to be executed, Lady Feng with disheveled hair and a filthy face came to the court hall and rebuked Rang: "Without sweat-of-the-horse merit you reached the rank of governor; you could not devote yourself fully to serving the state and repaying great grace, but instead violated the statutes and left booty scattered everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: As Rang was about to be executed, Lady Feng came to the court hall with disheveled hair and a filthy face and rebuked him: "Without sweat-of-the-horse merit you reached the rank of governor. You could not devote yourself fully to serving the state and repaying great grace, but instead violated the statutes and left booty scattered everywhere.

sentences.zh: 若言司馬誣汝，百姓百官不應亦皆誣汝。

translations.literal: If you say the Vice Governor slandered you, then the common people and hundred officials should not all have slandered you as well.
translations.idiomatic: If you say the Vice Governor slandered you, then the common people and hundred officials should not all have slandered you as well.

sentences.zh: 若言至尊不憐湣汝，何故治書覆汝？

translations.literal: If you say the Sovereign did not pity you, why did the Drafting Censor reinvestigate on your behalf?
translations.idiomatic: If you say the Sovereign did not pity you, why did the Drafting Censor reinvestigate on your behalf?

sentences.zh: 豈誠臣？

translations.literal: Are you a loyal minister?
translations.idiomatic: Are you a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 豈孝子？

translations.literal: Are you a filial son?
translations.idiomatic: Are you a filial son?

sentences.zh: 不誠不孝，何以為人！」

translations.literal: Neither loyal nor filial—how can you be called human!"
translations.idiomatic: Neither loyal nor filial—how can you be called human!

sentences.zh: 於是流涕嗚咽，親持盂粥勸讓令食。

translations.literal: She then wept with streaming tears, personally holding a bowl of gruel and urging Rang to eat.
translations.idiomatic: She then wept with streaming tears, personally holding a bowl of gruel and urging Rang to eat.

sentences.zh: 既而上表求哀，詞情甚切，上湣然為之改容。

translations.literal: She then submitted a memorial pleading for mercy, her words deeply moving; the emperor was touched and his expression changed.
translations.idiomatic: She then submitted a memorial pleading for mercy, her words deeply moving. The emperor was touched and his expression changed.

sentences.zh: 獻皇后甚奇其意，致請於上。

translations.literal: Empress Xian greatly admired her intent and interceded with the emperor on her behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian greatly admired her intent and interceded with the emperor on her behalf.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史柳彧進曰：「馮氏母德之至，有感行路。

translations.literal: Drafting Attendant Censor Liu Yu advanced and said: "Lady Feng's maternal virtue is supreme, moving even passersby on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Drafting Attendant Censor Liu Yu advanced and said, "Lady Feng's maternal virtue is supreme, moving even passersby on the road.

sentences.zh: 如或殺之，何以為勸？」

translations.literal: If he is executed, what example will that set?"
translations.idiomatic: If he is executed, what example will that set?
