sentences.zh: 上於是集京城士庶於硃雀門，遣舍人宣詔曰：「馮氏以嫡母之德，足為世范，慈愛之道，義感人神，特宜矜免，用獎風俗。

translations.literal: The emperor then gathered the gentry and commoners of the capital at Zhuque Gate and sent a palace attendant to proclaim an edict: "Lady Feng, with the virtue of a proper stepmother, is fit to be a model for the age; her path of loving kindness moves men and spirits through righteousness—she should specially be shown mercy, to reward good custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then gathered the gentry and commoners of the capital at Zhuque Gate and sent a palace attendant to proclaim an edict: "Lady Feng, with the virtue of a proper stepmother, is fit to be a model for the age. Her path of loving kindness moves men and spirits through righteousness. She should specially be shown mercy, to reward good custom.

sentences.zh: 讓可減死，除名為民。」

translations.literal: Rang's death sentence may be reduced; he is stripped of rank and made a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Rang's death sentence is reduced. He is stripped of rank and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 複下詔曰：「馮氏體備仁慈，夙閑禮度。

translations.literal: Another edict was issued: "Lady Feng embodies benevolence and kindness and has long been versed in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict was issued: "Lady Feng embodies benevolence and kindness and has long been versed in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 孽讓非其所生，往犯憲章，宜從極法。

translations.literal: The stepson Rang was not born of her, yet having violated the statutes he should receive the ultimate penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The stepson Rang was not born of her, yet having violated the statutes he should receive the ultimate penalty.

sentences.zh: 躬自詣闕，為之請命，匍匐頓顙。

translations.literal: She came personally to the palace to plead for his life, crawling and bowing her forehead to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: She came personally to the palace to plead for his life, crawling and bowing her forehead to the ground.

sentences.zh: 朕哀其義，特免死辜。

translations.literal: We pity her righteousness and specially exempt him from the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: We pity her righteousness and specially exempt him from the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 使天下婦人皆如馮者，豈不閨門雍睦，風俗和平！

translations.literal: If all women under Heaven were like Lady Feng, would not inner chambers be harmonious and customs peaceful!
translations.idiomatic: If all women under Heaven were like Lady Feng, would not inner chambers be harmonious and customs peaceful!

sentences.zh: 朕每嘉歎不能已。

translations.literal: We each time praise and sigh without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Each time We praise and sigh without cease.

sentences.zh: 宜標揚優賞，用章有德。

translations.literal: She should be publicly honored with generous reward, to manifest those who possess virtue.
translations.idiomatic: She should be publicly honored with generous reward, to manifest those who possess virtue.

sentences.zh: 可賜物五百段。」

translations.literal: She may be granted five hundred bolts of goods."
translations.idiomatic: She is granted five hundred bolts of goods.

sentences.zh: 集諸命婦，與馮相識，以寵異之。

translations.literal: All titled ladies were assembled to be introduced to Lady Feng, honoring her with special favor.
translations.idiomatic: All titled ladies were assembled to be introduced to Lady Feng, honoring her with special favor.

sentences.zh: ○劉昶女

translations.literal: ○ Daughter of Liu Chang
translations.idiomatic: Daughter of Liu Chang

sentences.zh: 劉昶女者，河南長孫氏之婦也。

translations.literal: The daughter of Liu Chang was the wife of the Zhangsun clan of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The daughter of Liu Chang was the wife of the Zhangsun clan of Henan.

sentences.zh: 昶在周，尚公主，官至柱國、彭國公，數為將帥，位望隆顯。

translations.literal: Chang in Zhou married a princess, rose to Pillar of State and Duke of Peng, served repeatedly as general, and his rank and prestige were lofty and eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Chang in Zhou married a princess, rose to Pillar of State and Duke of Peng, served repeatedly as general, and his rank and prestige were lofty and eminent.

sentences.zh: 與高祖有舊。

translations.literal: He had old ties with Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He had old ties with Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，甚親任，曆左武衛大將軍、慶州總管。

translations.literal: When the throne was received he was greatly trusted and favored, serving as General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard and Commander of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was received he was greatly trusted and favored, serving as General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Guard and Commander of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其子居士，為太子千牛備身，聚徒任俠，不遵法度，數得罪。

translations.literal: His son Jushi served as Personal Attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard for the Crown Prince, gathering followers and practicing knight-errantry, not observing the law, and repeatedly offending.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jushi served as Personal Attendant of the Thousand-Ox Guard for the Crown Prince, gathering followers and practicing knight-errantry, not observing the law, and repeatedly offending.

sentences.zh: 上以昶故，每輒原之。

translations.literal: Because of Chang, the emperor each time pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Chang, the emperor each time pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 居士轉恣，每大言曰：「男兒要當辮頭反縛，籧篨上作獠舞。」

translations.literal: Jushi grew ever more reckless, often declaring loudly: "A man ought to have his hair braided, be bound hand and foot, and dance the Liao dance upon a bamboo mat."
translations.idiomatic: Jushi grew ever more reckless, often declaring loudly, "A man ought to have his hair braided, be bound hand and foot, and dance the Liao dance upon a bamboo mat.

sentences.zh: 取公卿子弟膂力雄健者，輒將至家，以車輪括其頸而棒之。

translations.literal: He would take sons of grandees who were strong and robust, bring them to his house, encircle their necks with a cart wheel, and beat them with clubs.
translations.idiomatic: He would take sons of grandees who were strong and robust, bring them to his house, encircle their necks with a cart wheel, and beat them with clubs.

sentences.zh: 殆死能不屈者，稱為壯士，釋而與交。

translations.literal: Those who nearly died yet did not yield he called stalwarts, released them, and befriended them.
translations.idiomatic: Those who nearly died yet did not yield he called stalwarts, released them, and befriended them.

sentences.zh: 黨與三百人，其趫捷者號為餓鶻隊，武力者號為蓬轉隊。

translations.literal: His faction numbered three hundred; the swift were called the Hungry Falcon Company, the strong the Whirling Thistle Company.
translations.idiomatic: His faction numbered three hundred. The swift were called the Hungry Falcon Company, the strong the Whirling Thistle Company.

sentences.zh: 每韝鷹絏犬，連騎道中，毆擊路人，多所侵奪。

translations.literal: Each time he hooded hawks and leashed dogs, riding in file along the road, beating passersby and seizing much by force.
translations.idiomatic: Each time he hooded hawks and leashed dogs, riding in file along the road, beating passersby and seizing much by force.

sentences.zh: 長安市里無貴賤，見之者皆辟易，至於公卿妃主，莫敢與校者。

translations.literal: In the markets of Chang'an, high and low alike gave way at sight of him; even grandees' consorts and princesses dared not contend with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the markets of Chang'an, high and low alike gave way at sight of him. Even grandees' consorts and princesses dared not contend with him.

sentences.zh: 其女則居士之姊也，每垂泣誨之，殷勤懇惻。

translations.literal: His daughter was Jushi's elder sister; she always wept as she admonished him, earnest and deeply sincere.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was Jushi's elder sister. She always wept as she admonished him, earnest and deeply sincere.

sentences.zh: 居士不改，至破家產。

translations.literal: Jushi did not reform, until he ruined the family estate.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi did not reform until he ruined the family estate.

sentences.zh: 昶年老，奉養甚薄。

translations.literal: Chang was old, and his support was very meager.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was old, and his support was very meager.

sentences.zh: 其女時寡居，哀昶如此，每歸甯於家，躬勤紡績，以致其甘脆。

translations.literal: His daughter was then a widow; grieving for Chang in this state, each time she returned home to her parents she personally spun and wove to provide him delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was then a widow. Grieving for Chang in this state, each time she returned home to her parents she personally spun and wove to provide him delicacies.

sentences.zh: 有人告居士與其徒游長安城，登故未央殿基，南向坐，前後列隊，意有不遜，每相約曰：「當為一死耳。」

translations.literal: Someone reported that Jushi and his followers roamed Chang'an city, climbed the old foundation of Weiyang Palace, sat facing south with ranks arrayed before and behind, showing disrespectful intent, each saying to the other: "We ought to die for this."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Jushi and his followers roamed Chang'an city, climbed the old foundation of Weiyang Palace, sat facing south with ranks arrayed before and behind, showing disrespectful intent, each saying to the other, "We ought to die for this.

sentences.zh: 又時有人言居士遣使引突厥令南寇，當于京師應之。

translations.literal: At times someone also said Jushi sent envoys to bring the Turks south to raid, and that he would respond in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At times someone also said Jushi sent envoys to bring the Turks south to raid, and that he would respond in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上謂昶曰：「今日之事，當複如何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Chang: "In today's matter, what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Chang, "In today's matter, what is to be done?

sentences.zh: 昶猶恃舊恩，不自引咎，直前曰：「黑白在於至尊。」

translations.literal: Chang still relied on old favor, did not blame himself, and stepped forward saying: "Right and wrong lie with the Sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Chang still relied on old favor, did not blame himself, and stepped forward saying, "Right and wrong lie with the Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，下昶獄，捕居士党與，治之甚急。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious, imprisoned Chang, arrested Jushi's followers, and prosecuted them with great urgency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, imprisoned Chang, arrested Jushi's followers, and prosecuted them with great urgency.

sentences.zh: 憲司又奏昶事母不孝。

translations.literal: The judicial office also memorialized that Chang was unfilial toward his mother.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial office also memorialized that Chang was unfilial toward his mother.

sentences.zh: 其女知昶必不免，不食者數日，每親調飲食，手自捧持，詣大理餉其父。

translations.literal: His daughter knew Chang would surely not escape; she ate nothing for several days, yet each time personally prepared food, held it in her own hands, and went to the Court of Judicial Review to feed her father.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter knew Chang would surely not escape. She ate nothing for several days, yet each time personally prepared food, held it in her own hands, and went to the Court of Judicial Review to feed her father.

sentences.zh: 見獄卒，長跪以進，歔欷嗚咽，見者傷之。

translations.literal: Before the prison guards she knelt long to present it, sobbing and weeping; all who saw were moved to grief.
translations.idiomatic: Before the prison guards she knelt long to present it, sobbing and weeping. All who saw were moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 居士坐斬，昶竟賜死於家。

translations.literal: Jushi was executed by decapitation; Chang was ultimately granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Jushi was executed by decapitation. Chang was ultimately granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 詔百僚臨視。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred officials to witness it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the hundred officials to witness it.

sentences.zh: 時其女絕而復蘇者數矣，公卿慰諭之。

translations.literal: At that time his daughter had fainted and revived several times; grandees comforted and consoled her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time his daughter had fainted and revived several times. Grandees comforted and consoled her.

sentences.zh: 其女言父無罪，坐子以及於禍。

translations.literal: His daughter said her father was guiltless, punished because of his son.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter said her father was guiltless, punished because of his son.

sentences.zh: 詞情哀切，人皆不忍聞見。

translations.literal: Her words were mournful and piercing; none could bear to hear or see.
translations.idiomatic: Her words were mournful and piercing. None could bear to hear or see.

sentences.zh: 遂布衣蔬食以終其身。

translations.literal: She then wore coarse cloth and ate plain food to the end of her life.
translations.idiomatic: She then wore coarse cloth and ate plain food to the end of her life.

sentences.zh: 上聞而歎曰：「吾聞衰門之女，興門之男，固不虛也！」

translations.literal: When the emperor heard he sighed and said: "I have heard that daughters of a declining house and sons of a rising house—this is truly no empty saying!"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard he sighed and said, "I have heard that daughters of a declining house and sons of a rising house—this is truly no empty saying!"

sentences.zh: ○鐘士雄母

translations.literal: ○ Mother of Zhong Shixiong
translations.idiomatic: Mother of Zhong Shixiong

sentences.zh: 鐘士雄母者，臨賀蔣氏女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Zhong Shixiong was a daughter of the Jiang clan of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Zhong Shixiong was a daughter of the Jiang clan of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 士雄仕陳為伏波將軍。

translations.literal: Shixiong served Chen as General Who Calms the Waves.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong served Chen as General Who Calms the Waves.

sentences.zh: 陳主以士雄嶺南酋帥，慮其反覆，每質蔣氏於都下。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler, because Shixiong was a chieftain of Lingnan, feared he might turn traitor and each time held Lady Jiang as hostage in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler, because Shixiong was a chieftain of Lingnan, feared he might turn traitor and each time held Lady Jiang as hostage in the capital.

sentences.zh: 及晉王廣平江南，以士雄在嶺表，欲以恩義致之，遣蔣氏歸臨賀。

translations.literal: When Prince of Jin Yang Guang pacified Jiangnan, because Shixiong was in the Ling region he wished to win him through kindness and righteousness, and sent Lady Jiang back to Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guang, Prince of Jin, pacified Jiangnan, because Shixiong was in the Ling region he wished to win him through kindness and righteousness, and sent Lady Jiang back to Linhe.

sentences.zh: 既而同郡虞子茂、鐘文華等作亂，舉兵攻城，遣人召士雄，士雄將應之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Yu Zimao, Zhong Wenhua, and others of the same commandery rebelled, raised troops to attack the city, and sent men to summon Shixiong; Shixiong was about to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Yu Zimao, Zhong Wenhua, and others of the same commandery rebelled, raised troops to attack the city, and sent men to summon Shixiong. Shixiong was about to respond.

sentences.zh: 蔣氏謂士雄曰：「我前在揚都，備嘗辛苦。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang said to Shixiong: "I was formerly in Yangdu and fully tasted hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang said to Shixiong, "I was formerly in Yangdu and fully tasted hardship.

sentences.zh: 今逢聖化，母子聚集，沒身不能上報，焉得為逆哉！

translations.literal: Now we meet the sage transformation, mother and son reunited—even giving my life I could not repay this; how could I turn rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Now we meet the sage transformation, mother and son reunited—even giving my life I could not repay this. How could I turn rebel!

sentences.zh: 汝若禽獸其心，背德忘義者，我當自殺於汝前。」

translations.literal: If your heart is that of a beast, betraying virtue and forgetting righteousness, I shall kill myself before you."
translations.idiomatic: If your heart is that of a beast, betraying virtue and forgetting righteousness, I shall kill myself before you.

sentences.zh: 士雄於是遂止。

translations.literal: Shixiong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong then stopped.

sentences.zh: 蔣氏複為書與子茂等，諭以禍福。

translations.literal: Lady Jiang also wrote letters to Zimao and the others, instructing them on fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Jiang also wrote letters to Zimao and the others, instructing them on fortune and disaster.

sentences.zh: 子茂不從，尋為官軍所敗。

translations.literal: Zimao did not obey, and soon was defeated by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Zimao did not obey, and soon was defeated by government troops.

sentences.zh: 上聞蔣氏，甚異之，封為安樂縣君。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of Lady Jiang he greatly admired her and enfeoffed her as Lady of Anle county.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of Lady Jiang he greatly admired her and enfeoffed her as Lady of Anle county.

sentences.zh: 時尹州寡婦胡氏者，不知何氏妻也，甚有志節，為邦族所重。

translations.literal: At that time the widow Lady Hu of Yinzhou, wife of an unknown clan, possessed great resolve and integrity and was respected by her community.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the widow Lady Hu of Yinzhou, wife of an unknown clan, possessed great resolve and integrity and was respected by her community.

sentences.zh: 當江南之亂，諷諭宗黨，皆守險不從叛逆，封為密陵郡君。

translations.literal: During the turmoil of Jiangnan she admonished her clan, who all held the passes and refused to join the rebels; she was enfeoffed as Lady of Miling commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the turmoil of Jiangnan she admonished her clan, who all held the passes and refused to join the rebels. She was enfeoffed as Lady of Miling commandery.

sentences.zh: ○孝婦覃氏

translations.literal: ○ Filial Daughter-in-Law Lady Tan
translations.idiomatic: Filial Daughter-in-Law Lady Tan

sentences.zh: 孝婦覃氏者，上郡鐘氏婦也。

translations.literal: The filial daughter-in-law Lady Tan was the wife of the Zhong clan of Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The filial daughter-in-law Lady Tan was the wife of the Zhong clan of Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 與其夫相見未幾而夫死，時年十八。

translations.literal: She had not long been with her husband when he died; she was then eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: She had not long been with her husband when he died. She was then eighteen.

sentences.zh: 事後姑以孝聞。

translations.literal: She served her mother-in-law and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: She served her mother-in-law and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，姑及伯叔皆相繼而死，覃氏家貧，無以葬。

translations.literal: Within several years her mother-in-law and uncles all died in succession; the Tan family was poor and had no means to bury them.
translations.idiomatic: Within several years her mother-in-law and uncles all died in succession. The Tan family was poor and had no means to bury them.

sentences.zh: 於是躬自節儉，晝夜紡績，蓄財十年，而葬八喪，為州裡所敬，上聞而賜米百石，表其門閭。

translations.literal: She then personally practiced frugality, spinning day and night; saving for ten years she buried eight dead, was respected by her district, and when the emperor heard he granted a hundred shi of grain and honored her household gate.
translations.idiomatic: She then personally practiced frugality, spinning day and night. Saving for ten years she buried eight dead, was respected by her district, and when the emperor heard he granted a hundred shi of grain and honored her household gate.

sentences.zh: ○元務光母

translations.literal: ○ Mother of Yuan Wuguang
translations.idiomatic: Mother of Yuan Wuguang

sentences.zh: 元務光母者，范陽盧氏女也。

translations.literal: The mother of Yuan Wuguang was a daughter of the Lu clan of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The mother of Yuan Wuguang was a daughter of the Lu clan of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，造次以禮。

translations.literal: From youth she loved reading and in every circumstance observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: From youth she loved reading and in every circumstance observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 盛年寡居，諸子幼弱，家貧不能就學，盧氏每親自教授，勖以義方，世以此稱之。

translations.literal: In her prime she lived as a widow; her sons were young and weak, the family was poor and could not send them to school; Lady Lu personally taught them, exhorting them with moral principles, and the world praised her for this.
translations.idiomatic: In her prime she lived as a widow. Her sons were young and weak, the family was poor and could not send them to school. Lady Lu personally taught them, exhorting them with moral principles, and the world praised her for this.

sentences.zh: 仁壽末，漢王諒舉兵反，遣將綦良往山東略地。

translations.literal: At the end of Renshou Prince of Han Yang Liang raised troops in rebellion and sent General Qi Liang to seize territory in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Renshou Yang Liang, Prince of Han, raised troops in rebellion and sent General Qi Liang to seize territory in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 良以務光為記室。

translations.literal: Liang made Wuguang his secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Liang made Wuguang his secretary.

sentences.zh: 及良敗，慈州刺史上官政簿籍務光之家，見盧氏，悅而逼之，盧氏以死自誓。

translations.literal: When Liang was defeated, Governor of Cizhou Shangguan Zheng registered Wuguang's household; seeing Lady Lu he was pleased and tried to force her; Lady Lu vowed she would rather die.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was defeated, Shangguan Zheng, governor of Cizhou, registered Wuguang's household. Seeing Lady Lu he was pleased and tried to force her. Lady Lu vowed she would rather die.

sentences.zh: 政為人兇悍，怒甚，以燭燒其身。

translations.literal: Zheng was by nature fierce and brutal; enraged, he burned her body with candles.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was by nature fierce and brutal. Enraged, he burned her body with candles.

sentences.zh: 盧氏執志彌固，竟不屈節。

translations.literal: Lady Lu held to her resolve all the more firmly and ultimately did not yield her integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Lu held to her resolve all the more firmly and ultimately did not yield her integrity.

sentences.zh: ○裴倫妻

translations.literal: ○ Wife of Pei Lun
translations.idiomatic: Wife of Pei Lun

sentences.zh: 裴倫妻，河東柳氏女也，少有風訓。

translations.literal: The wife of Pei Lun was a daughter of the Liu clan of Hedong; from youth she had proper upbringing and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Pei Lun was a daughter of the Liu clan of Hedong. From youth she had proper upbringing and instruction.

sentences.zh: 大業末，倫為渭源令。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye Lun was magistrate of Weiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daye Lun was magistrate of Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 屬薛舉之亂，縣城為賊所陷，倫遇害。

translations.literal: During Xue Ju's rebellion the county seat was taken by bandits and Lun was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During Xue Ju's rebellion the county seat was taken by bandits and Lun was killed.

sentences.zh: 柳時年四十，有二女及兒婦三人，皆有美色。

translations.literal: Lady Liu was then forty, with two daughters and three daughters-in-law, all beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu was then forty, with two daughters and three daughters-in-law, all beautiful.

sentences.zh: 柳氏謂之曰：「我輩遭逢禍亂，汝父已死，我自念不能全汝。

translations.literal: Lady Liu said to them: "We have met with calamity and turmoil; your father is already dead; I myself think I cannot preserve you.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu said to them, "We have met with calamity and turmoil. Your father is already dead. I myself think I cannot preserve you.

sentences.zh: 我門風有素，義不受辱於群賊，我將與汝等同死，如何？」

translations.literal: Our family's integrity is established; by principle we cannot suffer disgrace from bandits—I intend to die together with you; what do you say?"
translations.idiomatic: Our family's integrity is established. By principle we cannot suffer disgrace from bandits. I intend to die together with you—what do you say?

sentences.zh: 其女等皆垂泣曰：「唯母所命。」

translations.literal: Her daughters all wept and said: "We obey whatever our mother commands."
translations.idiomatic: Her daughters all wept and said, "We obey whatever our mother commands.

sentences.zh: 柳氏遂自投于井，其女及婦相繼而下，皆重死于井中。

translations.literal: Lady Liu then threw herself into a well; her daughters and daughters-in-law followed one after another, all dying together in the well.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Liu then threw herself into a well. Her daughters and daughters-in-law followed one after another, all dying together in the well.

sentences.zh: ○趙元楷妻

translations.literal: ○ Wife of Zhao Yuankai
translations.idiomatic: Wife of Zhao Yuankai

sentences.zh: 趙元楷妻者，清河崔氏之女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Zhao Yuankai was a daughter of the Cui clan of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Zhao Yuankai was a daughter of the Cui clan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 父儦，在《文學傳》。

translations.literal: Her father Biao is recorded in the Literary Biographies.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Biao is recorded in the 《Literary Biographies》.

sentences.zh: 家有素範，子女皆遵禮度。

translations.literal: The family had established standards; sons and daughters all observed ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The family had established standards. Sons and daughters all observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 元楷父為僕射，家富於財，重其門望，厚禮以聘之。

translations.literal: Yuankai's father was a Vice Director; the family was rich in wealth and valued their clan prestige, sending rich gifts to betroth her.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai's father was a Vice Director. The family was rich in wealth and valued their clan prestige, sending rich gifts to betroth her.

sentences.zh: 元楷甚敬崔氏，雖在宴私，不妄言笑，進止容服，動合禮儀。

translations.literal: Yuankai greatly respected Lady Cui; even in private feasting he did not speak or laugh rashly; his comings and goings, bearing and dress always accorded with ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankai greatly respected Lady Cui. Even in private feasting he did not speak or laugh rashly. His comings and goings, bearing and dress always accorded with ritual.

sentences.zh: 化及之反也，元楷隨至河北，將歸長安。

translations.literal: When Huaji rebelled, Yuankai followed him to Hebei and was about to return to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji rebelled, Yuankai followed him to Hebei and was about to return to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 至滏口，遇盜攻掠，元楷僅以身免。

translations.literal: Reaching Fukou they met bandits who attacked and plundered; Yuankai barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Fukou they met bandits who attacked and plundered. Yuankai barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 崔氏為賊所拘，賊請以為妻，崔氏謂賊曰：「我士大夫女，為僕射子妻，今日破亡，自可即死。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was seized by bandits who asked her to be their wife; Lady Cui told the bandits: "I am a daughter of the scholar-official class, wife of a Vice Director's son; now that we are ruined I can simply die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was seized by bandits who asked her to be their wife. Lady Cui told the bandits, "I am a daughter of the scholar-official class, wife of a Vice Director's son. Now that we are ruined I can simply die at once.

sentences.zh: 遣為賊婦，終必不能。」

translations.literal: To be made a bandit's wife—I can never accept that."
translations.idiomatic: To be made a bandit's wife—I can never accept that.

sentences.zh: 群賊毀裂其衣，形體悉露，縛於床簀之上，將淩之。

translations.literal: The bandits tore her clothes, exposing her body entirely, bound her upon a bed mat, and were about to violate her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits tore her clothes, exposing her body entirely, bound her upon a bed mat, and were about to violate her.

sentences.zh: 崔氏懼為所辱，詐之曰：「今力已屈，當聽處分，不敢相違，請解縛。」

translations.literal: Lady Cui, fearing disgrace, deceived them, saying: "My strength is now broken; I will accept your disposition and dare not disobey—please untie me."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui, fearing disgrace, deceived them, saying, "My strength is now broken. I will accept your disposition and dare not disobey—please untie me.

sentences.zh: 賊遽釋之。

translations.literal: The bandits quickly released her.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits quickly released her.

sentences.zh: 崔因著衣，取賊佩刀，倚樹而立曰：「欲殺我，任加刀鋸。

translations.literal: Lady Cui then dressed, took a bandit's sword at his belt, and stood leaning against a tree, saying: "If you wish to kill me, apply blade and saw as you will.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui then dressed, took a bandit's sword at his belt, and stood leaning against a tree, saying, "If you wish to kill me, apply blade and saw as you will.

sentences.zh: 若覓死，可來相逼！」

translations.literal: If you seek my death, come and force me!"
translations.idiomatic: If you seek my death, come and force me!

sentences.zh: 賊大怒，亂射殺之。

translations.literal: The bandits were furious and shot her to death in a volley.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were furious and shot her to death in a volley.

sentences.zh: 元楷後得殺妻者，支解之，以祭崔氏之柩。

translations.literal: Later Yuankai captured his wife's killer, dismembered him, and offered the sacrifice at Lady Cui's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuankai captured his wife's killer, dismembered him, and offered the sacrifice at Lady Cui's coffin.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫稱婦人之德，皆以柔順為先，斯乃舉其中庸，未臻其極者也。

translations.literal: The historian says: In speaking of a woman's virtue, gentleness and compliance are always placed first—this merely cites the mean and does not reach the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: In speaking of a woman's virtue, gentleness and compliance are always placed first—this merely cites the mean and does not reach the utmost.

sentences.zh: 至於明識遠圖，貞心峻節，志不可奪，唯義所在，考之圖史，亦何世而無哉！

translations.literal: As for clear insight and far-reaching design, steadfast heart and lofty integrity, resolve that cannot be wrested away, righteousness as the sole guide—consult the chronicles and histories: in what age are such women absent!
translations.idiomatic: As for clear insight and far-reaching design, steadfast heart and lofty integrity, resolve that cannot be wrested away, righteousness as the sole guide—consult the chronicles and histories: in what age are such women absent!

sentences.zh: 蘭陵主質邁寒松，南陽主心逾匪石、洗媼孝女之忠壯，崔、馮二母之誠懇，足使義勇慚其志烈，蘭玉謝其貞芳。

translations.literal: Princess Lanling's substance surpassed the cold pine; Princess Nanyang's heart exceeded unyielding stone; the loyal valor of Lady Xi and the filial daughter; the sincere earnestness of the two mothers Cui and Feng—enough to make men of righteous courage ashamed of their own resolve, and orchids and jade yield before their chaste fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Lanling's substance surpassed the cold pine; Princess Nanyang's heart exceeded unyielding stone; the loyal valor of Lady Xi and the filial daughter; the sincere earnestness of the two mothers Cui and Feng—enough to make men of righteous courage ashamed of their own resolve, and orchids and jade yield before their chaste fragrance.

sentences.zh: 襄城、華陽之妃，裴倫、元楷之婦，時逢艱阻，事乖好合，甘心同穴，顛沛靡它，志勵冰霜，言逾皎日，雖《詩》詠共薑之自誓，《傳》述伯姬之守死，其將複何以加焉！

translations.literal: The consorts of Xiangcheng and Huayang, the wives of Pei Lun and Yuankai—meeting hardship and adversity, their unions cut short, content to share one grave, steadfast through turmoil without wavering, resolve hardened like frost and ice, words brighter than the clear sun—though the Odes sing of Jiang of Gong's vow, though the Documents relate Bo Ji guarding death unto the end, what could add to these deeds!
translations.idiomatic: The consorts of Xiangcheng and Huayang, the wives of Pei Lun and Yuankai—meeting hardship and adversity, their unions cut short, content to share one grave, steadfast through turmoil without wavering, resolve hardened like frost and ice, words brighter than the clear sun—though the 《Odes》 sing of Jiang of Gong's vow, though the 《Documents》 relate Bo Ji guarding death unto the end, what could add to these deeds!
